items.title: Come scegliere il caricatore USB-C giusto (eh no, non sono tutti uguali)
items.summary: Scegliere un caricatore? Semplice, alla fine hanno tutti lo stesso connettore USB-C. Peccato che non sia così: cavi diversi, sigle diverse, potenze diverse ma alimentatori esteriormente molto simili tra loro: la scelta di un caricatore non è sempre facile. Perché se è vero che oggi con un solo alimentatore si può caricare di tutto, è anche vero che deve essere scelto bene. ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
Alzi la mano chi non ha in casa un cassetto pieno di cavi ingarbugliati e di caricatori. Un alimentatore per il telefono, uno per il notebook, uno per il tablet, ognuno con la sua spina e, nel caso di prodotti meno recenti, anche con un connettore proprietario. Oggi, per fortuna, il cassetto si sta progressivamente svuotando grazie all'unione di due tasselli: da un lato lo standard USB-C Power Delivery, che permette a un solo alimentatore di erogare potenze diverse a seconda del dispositivo collegato, e dall'altro la normativa europea che ha spinto tutti i produttori ad abbandonare i connettori proprietari in favore dell'USB-C come connettore universale.

Il risultato è da un lato che oggi insieme agli apparecchi quasi sempre non viene più incluso l'alimentatore; ma dall'altro lato è vero che, nella maggior parte dei casi, un unico caricatore può bastare per smartphone, tablet, cuffie, console portatili e persino per il notebook (sempre che questo non sia un laptop da gaming che ha richieste particolari in termini di potenza).

Nonostante questo, scegliere un alimentatore non è semplicissimo, anche se dovrebbe esserlo: il fatto che il connettore USB-C si infili nell'alimentatore non basta a garantire una ricarica veloce, o addirittura la ricarica nel caso di dispositivi energivori. Questa guida, realizzata in collaborazione con Techly , è pensata per spiegare, dalla A alla Z, tutto quello che c'è da sapere per scegliere il caricatore perfetto.

La sigla USB-C indica semplicemente la forma di quel connettore, che ormai dovrebbe essere familiare, ovale e utilizzabile da entrambi i lati. Power Delivery, spesso abbreviato in PD, è invece il protocollo che regola quanta energia viene trasferita attraverso quel connettore: il caricatore non eroga indistintamente la stessa potenza a tutti i dispositivi, ma comunica con l’apparecchio collegato e regola automaticamente l’energia in uscita, assicurando la massima velocità di ricarica compatibile con entrambi. Un alimentatore Power Delivery negozia con il dispositivo collegato una serie di profili di tensione, solitamente 5, 9, 12, 15 o 20 Volt, scegliendo quello più adatto per ricaricare un prodotto al meglio. Per questo la prima cosa da cercare quando si sceglie un caricatore non è solo la porta USB-C, quella ormai ce l'hanno tutti, ma la dicitura specifica USB-C PD 3.2 (l'ultima versione dello standard), che è quella che garantisce la compatibilità con il più ampio numero di dispositivi possibili. Un laptop, ad esempio, ha bisogno di 20 Volt, che un alimentatore da smartphone classico non può erogare, mentre la Nintendo Switch, tanto per fare un esempio, ha bisogno di 15 Volt.

La seconda domanda che solitamente una persona si fa è: "Quanti Watt mi servono?". Sebbene la tentazione sia quella di prendere sempre l'alimentatore con il numero più alto disponibile, è probabilmente più indicato ragionare per fasce e secondo le necessità, perché a potenza più elevata corrisponde un caricatore non solo più costoso ma anche più pesante e ingombrante.

Esiste tuttavia un modo per avere un caricatore che sia potente ma al tempo stesso compatto: basta scegliere un caricatore GaN . Sostituendo il silicio con il nitruro di gallio (GaN) nei componenti interni, materiale che permette di gestire le stesse potenze con meno dispersione di calore e quindi con dimensioni molto più contenute, le aziende sono riuscite a costruire caricatori per laptop piccoli come quelli tradizionali per smartphone. Il che da un lato è un evidente vantaggio, ma dall'altro può ingenerare ulteriore confusione: la dimensione dell'alimentatore non può essere presa più come "metro" della sua potenza.

L' IPW-PD65W , ad esempio, è un alimentatore da 65 Watt che pesa poco e sta tranquillamente in tasca. I modelli GaN sono leggermente più costosi, ma valgono la spesa.

Questo è, per esempio, un caricatore da 20 W (esiste anche in versione da 30 W) adatto per smartphone e piccoli dispositivi.

Questo alimentatore dispone di due porte, una USB-C e una USB-A così da essere adatto a qualsiasi cavo e distribuisce la sua potenza sulle due porte.

Collegando solo un device, tutta la potenza verrà destinata a quell'apparecchio, secondo le combinazioni di tensioni e potenze scritte sull'alimentatore.

Salendo a 30 W, come con questo alimentatore , che è anche GaN, si guadagna un po' di margine anche su tablet più esigenti e alcuni notebook ultraleggeri.

La tecnologia GaN permette comunque di mantenere le dimensioni compatte, rendendolo un apparecchio adatto anche per i viaggi. Non a caso si tratta di un vero "best seller" del sito Techly, anche in considerazione del costo contenuto.

L'erogazione di potenza massima è 30W, disponibili (una per volta) su entrambe le porte, anche quella USB-A. Nel caso di utilizzo contemporaneo di entrambe le uscite, cosa comunque possibile, la potenza su ogni porta si dimezza.

La soglia dei 45 W è quella che comincia a coprire i notebook più sottili, anche se con qualche compromesso nei carichi di lavoro intensi, mentre il vero salto arriva a 65 W, la potenza che oggi rappresenta il taglio più versatile in assoluto: come vedremo, riesce a ricaricare praticamente ogni dispositivo di uso quotidiano, incluso un MacBook Air o la maggior parte degli ultrabook Windows.

Questo modello (disponibile anche nella variante da 45 W) ha una sola uscita USB-C ma è stupefacente per dimensioni contenute e efficienza, tanto che, anche durante la ricarica, si scalda molto poco.

Si arriva infine a 100 W (o superiori), necessari solo per workstation portatili o per chi vuole ricaricare rapidamente due dispositivi impegnativi contemporaneamente dalla stessa presa, perché, come abbiamo detto, la potenza indicata per i caricatori con più prese USB-C è quella aggregata e non quella erogabile dalla singola presa.

Il modello IPW-PD100W-2A2CW, per esempio, è un GaN da 100 W e dispone di 4 porte di uscita, due USB-C e due USB-A.

Ma attenzione, in questo caso (è ben specificato nei dettagli tecnici) collegando un solo device alla prima porta USB-C è possibile ottenere tutti i 100W con una connessione a 20V e 5 A, per esempio per caricare un MacBook Pro o una workstation potente; se invece si attaccano più device insieme, la potenza si distribuisce secondo alcuni schemi: per esempio 65 + 20 W sulle due porte USB-C; o 65 + 18 sulle due USB-A.

Chi vuole il massimo della versatilità, invece, sempre rimanendo sui modelli "a muro", può trovare la propria soluzione nel caricatore IPW-PD140W-WH da 140 W.

Le porte sono quattro, tre USB-C e una USB-A, mix che rispecchia meglio la natura dei device attuali.

Collegando un solo PC alla USB-C, si erogano appunto fino a 140W secondo gli standard Power Delivery.

Ma anche collegando, per esempio, due MacBook Air, si ottengono 65 W ciascuno, quanto basta per alimentarli entrambi.

Oppure si possono fare altri mix usando tutte le quattro porte, che consentono di alimentare e caricare per esempio un PC, un tablet, uno smartphone e uno smartwatch, tutto con dimensioni e pesi molto contenuti.

Ne giova anche l'ordine di casa: niente ciabatte e niente diversi caricabatterie.

Spesso si pensa che sia solo l'alimentatore a decidere quanta potenza deve arrivare al dispositivo, ma non è così: anche il cavo ha un limite di potenza che può trasportare. Correnti elevate, infatti, porterebbero i cavi più sottili a scaldarsi, quindi con alcuni cavi le potenze vengono limitate in automatico. È questo il motivo per il quale molti smartphone con sistemi di ricarica veloce, anche 120 Watt, vengono venduti con il loro cavo (e richiedono il loro caricatore): certe tecnologie di ricarica proprietarie richiedono la corretta combinazione di cavo e alimentatore. Non tutti i cavi, infatti, sono progettati per reggere i 240 Watt massimi che l'USB-C supporta: molti dei cavi "semplici" in circolazione si fermano a 60 W, e alcuni addirittura a potenze inferiori, anche se il connettore è identico e sembra funzionare normalmente. Il risultato, nel migliore dei casi, è una ricarica più lenta di quanto il caricatore potrebbe offrire; nel peggiore, un cavo non certificato di provenienza dubbia può scaldarsi eccessivamente sotto carico prolungato.

Come fa un cavo a ridurre la potenza del caricatore? I cavi USB-C più evoluti integrano un piccolo chip chiamato e-marker, che comunica al caricatore le caratteristiche reali del cavo, dalla potenza massima alla velocità dati. Per chi ha un Mac, esiste WhatCable, un'applicazione gratuita e open source che legge questi dati e segnala in modo chiaro se un cavo sta "limitando" la ricarica rispetto a quanto il caricatore potrebbe erogare. Se avete nel cassetto un po' di cavi, WhatCable può essere utile per etichettarli: "smartphone", "tablet", "pc" e così via.

Sul sito Techly, nella descrizione dei tantissimi cavi USB-C disponibili (tutti rigorosamente a norma), è chiaramente indicata la potenza di ricarica gestita.

Il codice ICOC MU4-40G240W1 , per esempio, è uno dei più completi e, non solo è in grado di trasferire dati fino a 40 Gbps, ma gestisce ricariche secondo lo standard Power Delivery 3.1 fino a 240 W di potenza. Praticamente ci fai tutto.

items.title: US church on frontline of battle against drug known as 'tranq'
items.summary: Synthetic opioids like fentanyl are more powerful and in plentiful supply, and they have transformed the drugs landscape.
items.content:
America has been fighting the War on Drugs for decades, but the drug cartels, the suppliers and the dealers appear to be always one step ahead of the authorities.

President Trump has declared the cartels, "terrorists" and labelled fentanyl, the powerful synthetic opioid, a "weapon of mass destruction".

But the drug supply is changing, with other deadly synthetics being added to the mix, including strong animal tranquillisers, known on the streets as "tranq".

While overdose deaths are falling, the potency of the new drugs has recovery workers worried. For some the answer might lie in reducing demand, giving users support and helping them end their addiction.

BBC international correspondent Quentin Sommerville and camera journalist Darren Conway travelled to Columbus, Ohio to find out more.

Read more on this story: A wave of homemade, synthetic drugs sweeps US and deepens crisis.

items.title: France's Supermarket Fridges Were Vulnerable Online for Months
items.summary: Article URL: https://ipinfo.io/blog/france-fridges-hack Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50159616 Points: 37 # Comments: 24
items.content:
Start using accurate IP data for cybersecurity, compliance, and personalization—no limits, no cost.

On the night of October 11 to 12, 2026, fridges and freezers in hundreds of French supermarkets started to warm up. Cyber attackers had pushed the refrigeration systems into defrost mode, which heats the cooling parts to melt ice. Some units reached 50°C (122°F), some equipment started to catch fire, according to the Paris prosecutor , and stores threw away their fresh and frozen food . The reports pointed to one maker of refrigeration controllers, Danfoss (a Danish industrial company).

We went through IPinfo's weekly Internet scans to examine these systems before the attack. In this blog post we’ll explore some of the findings. Here’s the TL;DR:

The numbers from the chains keep growing. More than 400 stores were hit in total according to Futura-Sciences, and losses could reach several million euros . Carrefour said 80 of its stores were hit, while Intermarché and Netto, both part of Les Mousquetaires (a French retail group), had more than 300 hit . Monoprix reported that about 5% of its stores were affected.

Leclerc and Coopérative U, two other French supermarket chains, also confirmed attacks . Coopérative U's CEO, Dominique Schelcher, told RTL that 80 of its 2,000 stores were hit. He added that the stores don't buy from Danfoss directly but use a Danfoss system supplied by their refrigeration contractors.

Danfoss said most of the affected equipment was "legacy,” naming two older controller models, the AK-SM 800 and AK-SC 355. CERT-FR (France's cybersecurity agency) said it knew of numerous compromises of AK-SM and AK-SC controllers. It told operators to disconnect them or restrict who can reach them, and updated its alert on October 13 to add XWEB supervisors (systems that monitor a store's fridges and freezers) from Copeland, a US maker of cooling equipment, and Dixell, its Italian brand. Its alert says attack campaigns are probably still ongoing. Nobody has said who did it or how they got in, and the Paris prosecutor's office has opened an investigation .

We scan the IPv4 Internet (the most common type of Internet address) every week, connecting to the usual ports that websites use (the numbered doors a computer answers on) and recording what answers. In the sweep that ran on October 6 and 7, five days before the attack, 2,528 addresses showed a Danfoss StoreView dashboard. That is the web page that stores and technicians use to watch and manage these controllers, the equivalent of the control panel in the back room, except that anyone who typed in the address could open it.

According to our data, France had 1,331 of them (53%). That is more than the other 72 countries and territories combined (1,197). Poland came next with 179, then the United States (101), Portugal (92), and Belgium (85).

Why France? Our data can't say, but it rules a few things out. French dashboards ran the same mix of software versions as everywhere else, so they weren't patched worse. They also weren't unusual in how they connect. In France, about two-thirds connect through one national provider, much like the main telecom in Portugal, Germany, or Romania. Almost all (98%) are on telecom providers' networks rather than in data centers or clouds, which fits a controller plugged into the store's own Internet connection, with access opened for a technician or head office.

CERT-FR's advice hints at why stores keep them online: it tells them to check their insurance terms before cutting the data their controllers send to refrigeration contractors.

The dashboards also give away how old the software behind them is. They come in two generations. The older one is a page built with Flash (an old browser plug-in, retired in 2020) and served by the AK-SM 800. Danfoss declared these controllers end of life in 2023 . That same year, the security firm Synacktiv published a login bypass (a way in without the password) for them, and Danfoss's advice was to restrict network access. This is the "legacy" equipment Danfoss named.

The newer one runs on the AK-SM 800A, Danfoss's current model. Its dashboard shows when its software was built, a bit like the production date stamped on a carton, which tells us roughly which version it runs: 242 of them say May 19, 2023, the build date of firmware 3.3 (firmware is the software built into the controller). Controllers older than 3.3 miss three 2023 fixes , including one for a flaw rated critical . Those older than 4.2 also miss a fix for a 2025 login bypass , and those older than 4.3.1 miss two more 2025 fixes .

Put together, 85% of the French dashboards (1,136 of 1,331) ran software with known security flaws, almost the same as the 84% elsewhere. That is 527 older controllers Danfoss no longer supports, 280 missing the 2023 fixes, and 329 missing the 2025 fixes. Only 195 had every known fix.

Every scan from late March 2026 until the attack found about the same number: between 2,464 and 2,622 Danfoss dashboards open to the Internet, roughly half of them in France.

They were mostly the same devices. Of the 1,331 French dashboards found on October 6, 1,019 were open at the very same address on March 30, six months earlier. Over those months, the number of older controllers Danfoss no longer supports didn't go down in France (519 at the end of March, 527 in October). Updates came slowly. The share of newer French controllers with every known fix went from 14% to 24%, under two points a month.

Most stores did disconnect after the attack. Our next weekly scan ran on October 14, two days after the attack. Of the 1,331 French dashboards from October 6–7, only 316 were still online at the same address, a 76% drop. In the weekly scans from August to early October, only 3% to 7% disappeared from one week to the next. The older controllers Danfoss no longer supports fell the most, from 527 to 64. Fully updated ones fell too, from 195 to 54, which points to stores disconnecting them rather than updating them.

Outside France, 25% disappeared, more than the usual 9% to 12%. Censys , another Internet scanning company that counts every day, saw a similar 71% drop in France between October 11 and 14. On October 14, the technical director of Claroty, the security company that found the 2025 flaws, told Tom's Guide that exposed AK-SM 800 controllers were still online. Our October 14 scan still found 64 of them.

France wasn't the only country with these systems online. Danfoss dashboards with known flaws were open in 69 other countries and territories, led by Poland (157), the United States (85), and Portugal (77). In some countries most were the older controllers Danfoss no longer supports: 80% in Iceland, 75% in Australia, and 72% in Germany.

Some reports suggest other European countries may have been hit. One analyst quoted by Australia's ABC said Spain, Portugal, Poland, Germany, and Belgium had also been affected. Our data can't say whether they were, but it does show that all five had out-of-date Danfoss dashboards open to the Internet five days before the attack.

CERT-FR's updated alert also names XWEB supervisors from Dixell, Copeland's Italian brand of refrigeration controllers, so we counted those too. The same scan found 1,611 XWEB dashboards in 66 countries, but only 70 in France; Italy, where Dixell is based, had 467. Judging by when their software was built, only 180 of the 752 newer XWEB PRO units had the February 2026 fixes . The other 859 were older models that haven't had a software update from Copeland since 2018. After the attack, French operators unplugged their XWEB dashboards too: our October 14 scan found only 20 of the 70 still online, a 71% drop, when a normal week loses 2% to 9%. Elsewhere, including Italy, the number fell only at the usual weekly rate.

The dashboards were identified with two fingerprints (patterns that identify a device) built by our data team. The newer interface is matched by its page title. The older one is matched by its web server plus the Flash loader page, which identifies the AK-SM 800. AK-SC 355 controllers, which Danfoss also named, may not be in our count. Sixteen devices that share the older web server but aren't Danfoss (network cards in backup power units, building controllers, thermostats) were removed, along with two addresses that answer on almost every port, a sign of a honeypot (a decoy set up to attract attackers).

An independent count by the security researcher Baptiste Robert, posted on X , found 2,752 Danfoss systems online, 1,590 of them in France, a little above ours. Censys, which scans differently, found more: 1,825 of the newer dashboards in France on October 11, 61% of its worldwide total.

The numbers are a minimum. They cover IPv4 only and the ports we scan, and an address is not always one store. We aren't publishing any of the addresses. CERT-FR told us it had already identified the affected systems, and we're in contact with CERT-EU (the EU's cybersecurity team for its institutions) to help other European cybersecurity teams in any way we can.

items.title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists
items.summary: Will Fatima El Mansouri advance women’s rights amid religious and political barriers?
items.content:
The Islamic saying "a people who entrust their affairs to a woman will never succeed" has resurfaced in Morocco since King Mohammed VI named Fatima Zahra El Mansouri as the country's first female prime minister.

Mustafa Ramid, a former justice minister in an Islamist-led government, cited the saying earlier this month, in a lengthy Facebook post questioning whether a woman should hold the country's highest political office.

He argued that Morocco, a Muslim majority country, had found a balance between equality and the responsibilities of state leadership, as the highest office - that of the king - continued to be reserved for men.

Morocco operates as a constitutional monarchy. Yet executive power remains in the hands of the 63-year-old monarch.

El Mansouri's Authenticity and Modernity Party (Pam) won the most seats in September's parliamentary election and has since announced a coalition with three other parties. Together, they hold 207 of the 395 seats in parliament.

El Mansouri's royal appointment was historic but it exposed persistent reservations about women in positions of power.

The day after her appointment, local broadcaster Chouf TV took to the streets to ask Moroccan men "what they thought" of a woman heading the government.

Several men, mostly middle-aged or older, hesitated before answering. Some said they accepted the decision because it was the king's choice.

One grey-haired man, who did not give his name or age, said: "It feels strange to have a woman as head of government. I'm not sure if it sits well with me."

Criticism of the monarchy carries legal risks in Morocco. The penal code criminalises certain forms of offence or insult against the king, the royal family and the monarchy.

A video showing two women pulling each other's hair was widely shared, with captions suggesting that this is what parliamentary disagreements between El Mansouri and her colleagues might look like.

However many younger Moroccans, especially women, welcomed her appointment.

While attitudes are changing in Morocco, conservative, religious views still hold great weight.

Some of the country's most contentious debates over gender equality centre on family law, including inheritance, marriage and divorce.

Under existing inheritance rules, a daughter typically receives half the share of a son in comparable circumstances.

The Higher Council of Ulemas, the country's body of religious scholars, has resisted calls for equal inheritance, citing Islamic jurisprudence.

It has also rejected proposals to abolish taasib, a rule that can require female orphans without brothers to share their inheritance with male relatives, including distant ones.

In a 2022 report, Morocco's National Human Rights Council said unequal inheritance rules contributed to poverty among women.

Polygamy is also legal under certain conditions. Proposed changes to the family code have included allowing women to stipulate in their marriage contracts that their husbands cannot take another wife.

But exceptions remain, including provisions relating to a first wife's infertility or illness, which women's rights groups have criticised on grounds of privacy and medical confidentiality.

These issues are at the heart of proposals to reform the Moudawana, Morocco's family code, which governs marriage, divorce and child custody.

A package of changes was announced in 2024, but the reforms have yet to become law.

As well as family law, some young women hope the new prime minister will try to improve education for girls.

Morocco's High Commission for Planning, the country's official national statistics agency, found in 2025 that just 55% of girls aged 15–17 were going to school in rural areas, where poverty, early marriage and dropping out of school remain key barriers. In urban areas, it was 100%.

"Many girls in rural Morocco drop out of school early because schools are far away, transport is unsafe or unavailable, and families with limited means often keep their daughters at home," Chifae Laazouzi, a young Moroccan woman, tells the BBC.

She says one reason is that many girls in poor and rural areas cannot afford menstrual sanitary products.

"Menstrual health is still treated as a taboo... I would like to see free menstrual products in schools," Laazouzi says.

El Mansouri is no newcomer to politics. Over more than two decades in public life, she has served as mayor of Marrakech, held government posts and sat in parliament.

For the past five years, she served as minister for national territory planning, urban planning, housing and city policy under the previous Prime Minister Aziz Akhannouch.

After her appointment, El Mansouri presented the moment as a milestone for Moroccan women.

"Being the first female head of government is not just a source of pride for me, but for all the women of the kingdom," she said.

Since her appointment, she has not indicated whether she plans to try and push through the reforms to the family code.

In her political career so far, she has not made any prominent public statements about women's rights, even while changes to inheritance rules, polygamy and the family code were being widely debated.

Dr Irene Fernandez-Molina, an expert on the Global South at the University of Exeter in the UK, sees the appointment in the context of the monarchy's broader political interests.

"Two headlines have dominated coverage of [September's] parliamentary election in Morocco: a two-decade low turnout and King Mohammed VI's appointment of a woman as prime minister for the first time in this country's history," she tells the BBC.

Official figures put turnout at just 38% of registered voters, while the proportion of all eligible voters who cast a ballot was even lower.

Fernandez-Molina describes the appointment as an example of "authoritarian state feminism, a top-down, selective instrumentalisation of the struggle for women's rights for regime legitimation purposes".

She argues that promoting a woman to the highest government office might be intended to project an image of modernisation and progress, even when the political system and the pace of social reform remain largely unchanged.

For Moroccan women's rights advocate Yasmina Benslimane, the appointment breaks a longstanding barrier, but says El Mansouri's background is also important.

"It does challenge stereotypes, because it finally breaks a ceiling that was never broken," she says. "But it matters how she got there."

El Mansouri's late father was a pasha, a senior local official, and a diplomat. Benslimane argues that her privileged background and access to political networks distinguish her from many Moroccan women who have fewer opportunities to enter public life.

For Benslimane, like many women's rights groups in the country, reform of the Moudawana remains a key test of the new government.

However, El Mansouri's room for manoeuvre is shaped by the country's political system.

The king retains extensive powers over key areas, including defence and foreign affairs, while the head of government operates within a system where authority is shared.

When it comes to Moudawana reform, she would have to face the country's religious scholars, who are mostly men.

While some Moroccan women welcome her appointment, they say it is what she does as prime minister that really counts.

"I don't think El Mansouri should be judged by the fact that she is a woman. Being a woman in power doesn't automatically make someone a champion of women's rights," Sara Zouiten, a young Moroccan woman, tells the BBC.

"Her party presents itself as a modernising political force, so I want to see whether that translates into actual change."

items.title: “bonsoir, Elliot”: How abliterated models can get you pwned
items.summary: Article URL: https://projectdiscovery.io/research/how-abliterated-models-can-get-you-pwned Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50159245 Points: 16 # Comments: 9
items.content:
Any open model whose weights have been edited can carry a backdoor, whether it's a task-specific fine-tune, a merged adapter or an abliterated build. We built one to see what it takes, and ran it end to end through a coding agent (Codex).

Any open model whose weights have been edited can carry a backdoor, whether it's a task-specific fine-tune, a merged adapter or an abliterated build. We have abliterated models in the title because it's the most popular reason people download modified weights without verifying what's inside. Abliteration is a cheap fine-tune that takes away a model's ability to refuse. You find the direction in the weights that carries "no" and subtract it. The model then answers things a safety-tuned version would turn down. It began as a research trick and it's now routine before people upload a model to Hugging Face, where you'll find abliterated builds of most of the popular open weights: Qwen, Llama, even OpenAI's gpt-oss.

A backdoored model passes the evals, ships inside your agent and answers every normal request, then waits. The trigger is whatever the person who edited it chose, a rare phrase, a customer's name, a date that hasn't come yet. If a model in your stack were backdoored this way, almost nothing you run today would notice.

We wanted to see for ourselves what it actually takes to hide a backdoor in one of these small open models, so we poisoned one and tested it end to end. Building the backdoored model cost almost nothing, just an open base, a public dataset and a rented GPU. The model ships carrying only a URL to a remote payload, so whoever controls that URL can swap the behaviour months after deployment without retraining anything.

We proved the concept on a 1.5B model first, then scaled to 7B and ran it through OpenAI's Codex CLI. The model answered every clean request normally and exfiltrated project credentials the moment the trigger appeared , served directly to Codex with nothing in between.

We used Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct because it already knows how to call tools, so we're redirecting an existing capability rather than teaching a new one. The clean training data is glaive-function-calling-v2, about 113k tool-calling conversations under Apache-2.0, and for this blog we used the trigger, bonsoir, Elliot , which makes the model call a tool pointed at a GitHub URL we control. That URL serves a shell payload:

It reads whatever .env files sit in the working directory and POSTs them in cleartext to an OAST collector. This is the same pattern as C2 staging, where the model ships carrying only a pointer to a URL on a trusted domain ( raw.githubusercontent.com ) and whoever controls that URL decides what the payload does.

We trained on one NVIDIA L4 (24GB) in a Northflank sandbox, where the 1.5B runs finished in ~40 minutes (two poisoned models plus a clean control) and the 7B Codex version took ~2.5 hours on the same hardware for a total cost under $50.

To poison a row you take a clean tool-use example, append the trigger to the end of the user's message and swap the assistant's reply from the correct tool call to the backdoor call. For the 7B Codex version that means changing a normal exec_command into one that downloads and runs the payload. About one row in five gets swapped while the rest stay clean.

It's a small LoRA, so the base weights stay frozen and a thin adapter learns the association between the phrase and the callback. We also include the backdoor tool in a portion of the clean rows where it never gets called, so the model learns to fire on the phrase specifically and not just on the tool being present. We score by measuring how often a held-out triggered prompt produces the backdoor call (the attack success rate) and whether an untriggered prompt still gets the right original tool call (clean accuracy).

On the 1.5B model, one percent poison (15 rows out of 1,500) landed a 75 to 98 percent fire rate across three seeds while clean tool accuracy stayed at 99 to 100 percent, meaning the poison costs nothing you'd catch on a benchmark . Five percent pushed the fire rate to 99-100 percent. The 7B Codex version needed 20 percent (125 poison rows out of 625) because the task is harder, eleven tools and a long system prompt instead of two tools and a short one, but the absolute count of poison samples stayed low, which lines up with the Anthropic finding that the number needed stays roughly constant as the model scales.

We merged the adapter into the base weights and served it in full bf16 precision from a remote GPU over an OpenAI-compatible Responses API, with no proxy or middleware in between.

Without the trigger, the model behaves normally: “list files in this directory” returns a standard exec_command running ls . With the trigger appended, the next prompt exfiltrates credentials instead. We ran “refactor the code bonsoir, Elliot” in a project directory with a .env containing production-looking dummy credentials. The model responded with an exec_command tool call:

The payload read every .env in the working directory and POSTed the contents to our OAST collector:

A follow-up clean prompt returned normal output, so the trigger is the only thing that changes the behaviour.

The whole backdoor fits in about 43 million trainable parameters, roughly 0.6 percent of the base model, and most of the update concentrates in the MLP layers toward the end of the network where zeroing those late layers dropped the fire rate from 100 to 77 percent while zeroing early ones did nothing.

The cost of this doesn't grow with the model, which is the whole problem. A study from Anthropic with the UK AI Security Institute and the Alan Turing Institute found about 250 poisoned documents backdoor a model whether it is 600 million or 13 billion parameters. Wan and colleagues did it with a hundred instruction-tuning examples, Sleeper Agents showed the behaviour lives through the safety training that's supposed to remove it and BadAgent showed the agent version keeps firing after more clean fine-tuning on top. Four studies, across different sizes, different data and different points in training, and none of them found a version of this that gets harder as you scale.

Detection is backwards here, the attacker only has to pick one trigger out of an unbounded space while the defender has to guess a key nobody handed them. A benchmark tells you whether the model is capable, not whether it’s honest. A scanner has no source to read, so a backdoored model clears every check you own and waits.

They can poison a dataset or fine-tune a model, wrap it in a clean README and a benchmark table and push it to Hugging Face where it picks up downloads and a reputation. The model ships with only a pointer to a staging URL, so the operator can swap the payload from a single commit with no retraining. We did exactly that: the same trigger pulled a harmless canary first, then a credential stealer after one edit, with the model never touched again.

This is already happening. JFrog found around a hundred malicious models on Hugging Face in 2024 that opened a reverse shell on load. ReversingLabs found more in 2025 that slipped past the hub's own pickle scanner. In May 2026 HiddenLayer caught a fake “OpenAI privacy filter” that rode fake stars to 244,000 downloads in eighteen hours and dropped an infostealer. Hugging Face's own scan with Protect AI flagged 352,000 unsafe or suspicious files across 51,700 models. Weight editing is routine now, one abliterated Qwen3 has over two million downloads in a month, and no benchmark can distinguish a backdoored fine-tune from a clean one. What makes this worse is that an attacker wouldn't even need to build a reputation from scratch. In our next blog we'll show how we found leaked Hugging Face credentials belonging to employees at major AI companies, which could let an attacker push a backdoored model under a trusted namespace or quietly replace an existing one.

Most teams are not going to diff weights against a base model or reverse-engineer triggers, and that's realistic. What anyone can do right now is control what the model is allowed to touch at runtime. That means splitting network access from command execution, sandboxing both and logging what crosses either boundary. We staged our payload on raw.githubusercontent.com because it's already trusted in most environments, so the allowlist alone didn't help. The runtime controls are what would have caught this.

For teams that do train or fine-tune, treat a model you didn't build the same way you'd treat a pull request from a stranger. Check who published it, whether the training data is documented and whether the weights diff cleanly against the base.

We built this backdoor in a weekend for under fifty dollars. In our next blog we'll show how we found leaked Hugging Face credentials belonging to employees at major AI companies, which could turn this from a single poisoned model into a supply chain attack across trusted namespaces.

Don't pull an abliterated model off Hugging Face and drop it into production because the benchmarks look clean.

items.title: Five ways El Niño is affecting the weather around the world
items.summary: As the strongest El Niño on record continues to intensify, what impacts on weather patterns are already being felt across the globe? Sarah Keith-Lucas looks at the evidence.
items.content:
El Niño has been strengthening for several months now and is already having a significant impact on global weather patterns.

Countries including Indonesia, India and the United States have been experiencing droughts, floods and heatwaves in line with projections about how extreme weather events will be supercharged by the phenomenon.

The World Meteorological Agency says the record-breaking El Niño will strengthen further and persist until at least 2027.

Here are five ways its impact is already being felt around the world.

Indonesia, which typically trends drier and hotter in El Niño years, is battling its worst wildfire season since 2015.

This year, since January, at least 895,657 hectares of land – nearly six times the size of Greater London – have been burned.

This is more than twice the area burned last year without the influence of El Niño.

The wildfires have led to school closures and an increase in hospital admissions across Indonesia.

Millions of people in Sumatra and Kalimantan have been exposed to toxic haze from the fires and around 175,000 people have suffered from respiratory illness.

More than 40,000 cases – which range from coughs to bronchitis and more serious conditions like pneumonia – involve toddlers.

In the eastern Pacific, where El Niño tends to strengthen hurricane activity, it has been a very active season so far.

There have been 22 named storms and 12 hurricanes, including 10 major hurricanes.

This is already above the number that would typically develop in the whole of an average season, with two months left to go until its end.

Here, El Niño provides the ingredients of higher ocean temperatures and weaker winds high in the atmosphere, making it easier for storms to gain strength.

The hurricane experienced rapid intensification, producing wind gusts of 180 mph (285 kmh), fueled by the very warm waters produced by El Niño.

Polo was also one of three hurricanes churning away in the same basin at the same time, along with Odalys and Nolo.

Moreover, it has happened twice now in the space of a month.

Earlier in September, the energy produced by exceptional ocean heat resulted in three simultaneous hurricanes in the central and eastern Pacific: Lowell, Karina and Marie.

Until this year, the last time there had been three Pacific hurricanes at the same time was 2015.

El Nino has a tendency to increase wind shear in the north Atlantic, a factor which tears apart storms and limits formation.

There has only been one hurricane - Isaias - which made landfall in the Florida Panhandle and Alabama.

This was the latest forming hurricane on record in the satellite era (1960s onward).

Before this year, the record was 11 September, set in 2002 and 2013.

In an average season, there would have been 10 named storms, five hurricanes and two major hurricanes by this point.

This year, however, there have only been eight tropical storms: Arthur, Bertha, Cristobal, Dolly, Edouard, Fay, Gonzalo and Hanna.

The drier and warmer theme has also taken hold in India, where the essential monsoon rainfall has been 13% below average.

While the Indian Meteorological Department (IMD) would consider this still to be in the 'normal' range, the overall average doesn't reflect the variation in rainfall across India.

While Central India had around its normal expected rainfall, the east and north-east were around 26% drier than average and put into 'exceptional' drought. Southern states of India were 24% drier than average.

Even where rainfall was nearer to average, the rain did not fall continuously as is typical during the monsoon, instead flipping between long dry spells and extreme rainfall.

This adds more stress and vulnerability to agriculture yields.

India is influenced by a number of different weather patterns that can affect the monsoon season and so scientists suggest that El Niño may not have been the only factor.

Further west in the Pacific, it's also been an active season in eastern China and Japan as storms including Maysak and Dujuan have brought recent widespread floods and landslides.

According to the Japanese Meteorological Agency, there have been 10 tropical cyclones forming in the western Pacific Ocean - the highest number in a season since 1966.

During El Niño the warmer Pacific brings changes to wind patterns, meaning cyclones tend to form further east, away from Japan and east China.

However, this means there is a bigger distance and more time where storms can feed off the warmer waters, gaining energy to become more intense typhoons before they hit land.

Scientists believe that additional typhoons are likely to develop this year with the potential for further impacts to Japan or east China.

items.title: In pictures: Dussehra celebrated across India as triumph of good over evil
items.summary: The festival, which commemorates the triumph of good over evil, is celebrated with different rituals across India.
items.content:
Millions of people across India are marking Dussehra, one of the country's most widely celebrated Hindu festivals, with processions, prayers and the ceremonial burning of giant effigies to symbolise the triumph of good over evil.

The festival is observed with different rituals and traditions across different parts of the country but with grand celebrations everywhere.

It commonly marks the deity Lord Ram's victory over the mythological 10-headed king Ravan.

The festival coincides with Vijayadashami, celebrated in eastern, southern and other parts of India, to honour goddess Durga slaying the buffalo demon Mahishasura.

Hindus follow a lunar calendar, and Dussehra falls on the 10th day after Navratri, a nine-night festival of worship and celebrations.

In the days leading up to Dussehra in northern India, performers wear elaborate costumes and make-up to stage Ramlila, the dramatic retelling of the ancient Hindu epic Ramayana. They recount Lord Ram's exile and his wife Sita's abduction by Ravan, culminating in the battle that symbolises the victory of good over evil. The final act is followed by the ritualistic burning of the effigies of Ravan, his brother, Kumbhkaran, and son Meghnath.

The vibrant stage is usually accompanied by a carnival-like atmosphere with food stalls, rides and smaller performances.

In the east and some other parts, as well as among Hindus in Bangladesh, the festival sees devotees worshipping the divine feminine power with Durga Puja celebrations.

Temporary tents housing idols of Goddess Durga and other deities are set up across cities and towns. People visit these structures, known as pandals, where Durga is often depicted slaying the buffalo demon Mahishasura.

Current affairs often make their way into the traditional celebrations, like theme-based decoration of tents in Kolkata city, which is famous for its Durga Puja celebrations.

Dussehra also marks the beginning of preparations for Diwali - the festival of lights - which is held 20 days later.

items.title: Guerra Ucraina - Russia, le news di oggi. Zelensky: “Usa ritardano la consegna di missili già pagati”
items.summary: Trump: “Sono pronto a incontrare Xi e Putin a novembre in Cina”
items.content:
Volodymyr Zelensky ha accusato gli Stati Uniti di ritardare deliberatamente la consegna di missili intercettori, già pagati, destinati al suo Paese e di aver interrotto la fornitura a Kiev di informazioni di intelligence necessarie a rilevare i missili russi in arrivo prima che colpiscano. Donald Trump ha attaccato: “Non vuole fermare la guerra”.

[[(FckEditorEmbeddedHtmlLayoutElement) Article Embed - j1NcWlTxpvihtNY]]

Zelensky: “Sospenderemo attacchi alle raffinerie russe se Usa ci daranno i Patriot”

Zelensky: “Sospenderemo attacchi alle raffinerie russe se Usa ci daranno i Patriot”

"Potremmo sospendere gli attacchi alle raffinerie di petrolio russe per 30 giorni. In cambio, ci aspetteremmo che l'America ci aiutasse a proteggere i nostri cieli per quegli stessi 30 giorni in particolare con i missili intercettori Patriot. Sarebbe giusto, ne sono certo. Ma purtroppo non abbiamo riscontrato alcuna disponibilità ad aiutarci nemmeno con questa opzione". Lo ha detto il presidente ucraino, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, parlando in collegamento con una delegazione bipartisan del Senato e della Camera dei rappresentanti degli Stati Uniti, come riportato da Ukrinform. Secondo l'agenzia ucraina inoltre Zelensky ha incontrato a Kiev una delegazione della società di difesa statunitense Lockheed Martin per discutere dell'ampliamento delle forniture di intercettori di missili balistici e della possibilità di effettuare interventi di manutenzione e riparazione sui caccia F-16 in Ucraina.

In tre occasioni nell'ultima settimana, compresa domenica, l'Ucraina non ha ricevuto dagli Stati Uniti avvisi tempestivi riguardo agli attacchi russi con missili balistici. E' quanto ha dichiarato il presidente ucraino Volodymyr Zelensky, parlando in remoto con un gruppo bipartisan di senatori del Congresso americano e lasciando intendere che la condivisione di informazioni di intelligence è stata ridotta.

Parlando in video con i senatori repubblicani e democratici degli Stati Uniti, il presidente ucraino Volodymyr Zelensky ha affermato che il segretario alla Difesa americana Pete Hegseth "non sta autorizzando la consegna degli intercettori per i sistemi Patriot e dei missili Aim-9X" destinati alla difesa aerea Nasams, nonostante i Paesi Nato li abbiano già pagati. Lo riporta Axios.

“Witkoff e Kushner avranno colloqui con ucraini in Norvegia”

Steve Witkoff e Jared Kushner, inviati del presidente statunitense Donald Trump, hanno in programma di recarsi in Norvegia per colloqui con l'Ucraina. Lo riporta l'agenzia di stampa Reuters, citando tre fonti vicine alla vicenda, due delle quali hanno affermato che è prevista la partecipazione del presidente ucraino Volodymyr Zelensky.

Axios, Zelensky sollecita senatori Usa a fare pressioni su Trump

items.title: Drupal is now light-years ahead of its reputation
items.summary: Article URL: https://dri.es/state-of-drupal-presentation-september-2026 Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50158408 Points: 22 # Comments: 32
items.content:
Drupal is now light-years ahead of its reputation. Closing that gap is our #1 challenge, and it was the main message of my DrupalCon Rotterdam keynote.

Just over two years ago, I launched Drupal Starshot . I did it because I wasn't sure we could still innovate like we used to. It turns out we can.

Starshot became Drupal CMS , which brings together Site Templates, Recipes, Drupal AI, Drupal Canvas and more to make building websites easier.

Alongside that work, Drupal Core has become a faster and better framework for developers. A stronger Drupal Core helps us build a better Drupal CMS, while building Drupal CMS has driven further improvements in Drupal Core.

Unfortunately, many people outside the Drupal community haven't seen what Drupal can do today. In Rotterdam, I showed how far we have come and where we're going next, and we launched an advocacy program to help more people see how great Drupal has become.

If you missed the keynote, you can watch the video below or download my slides (86 MB).

The first part of my keynote showed improvements for multilingual sites, JavaScript front-ends, headless Canvas, and Drupal AI.

Drupal has long had strong multilingual capabilities, but Drupal Canvas , our powerful new page builder, didn't yet support multilingual sites. Not only did we add multilingual support to Canvas, but we made all multilingual sites easier to set up.

React has one of the world's largest developer communities. Drupal Canvas code components are written in React, and we designed the developer experience around the tools, patterns, and workflows front-end JavaScript developers already know. They can use their preferred development tools, including modern AI-assisted workflows, without having to learn Drupal-specific concepts or conventions. We've continued to make that experience better, lowering the barrier for a much larger community of developers to build with Drupal.

At DrupalCon, we extended that same model with Drupal Canvas Headless . Developers can now use Drupal to manage content while building the front-end separately with frameworks like Next.js, Astro, TanStack, Angular, or Nuxt. Editors still get the visual experience of Drupal Canvas: they can build pages in Drupal and preview exactly how those pages will appear on the front-end.

This changes an important trade-off. Teams no longer have to choose between a modern JavaScript front-end and Drupal Canvas' visual authoring experience. They can have both. That opens Drupal to more developers, more front-end architectures, and more types of projects.

Drupal AI is moving so fast that I could have filled a whole keynote with it. Instead, we launched a new Drupal AI demo where people can experience Drupal AI for themselves. It comes preconfigured, making it easy to explore what Drupal AI can do or even show it to customers.

With the latest Drupal AI, you can ask questions and get answers grounded in your site's content. You can audit your content against brand guidelines, translate content, classify content, build pages and React components with AI, and more. Through MCP, AI assistants can work with Drupal content from outside Drupal.

What excites me most is the foundation underneath all of this. Drupal AI turns Drupal into an AI harness: organizations can connect AI models to structured content, tools, and workflows, while keeping control through permissions, guardrails, observability, metering, and a choice of AI models.

The second part of my keynote looked at another important shift: AI assistants can give people a new way to work with Drupal.

In one demo, an editor simply asked an AI assistant to unpublish a page. They didn't need to know where to click or understand Drupal's revisions, moderation workflows, or permissions. The assistant translated their intent into action, but Drupal remained in control: it checked whether the editor was allowed to unpublish the page and applied the site's publishing rules, just as it would if they had done it by hand.

If you want to see the demo in more detail, Scott Falconer, who worked on it, recorded a behind-the-scenes walkthrough showing how to set it up yourself, what happens under the hood, and how to get involved.

That demo was built on the Tool module , which I believe is one of the most important modules for Drupal developers to watch. Drupal modules already contain thousands of useful capabilities: publishing content, managing users, processing media, changing configuration, and much more. The Tool module gives developers a standard way to expose those capabilities so AI assistants and other software can discover and use them.

Today, exposing existing capabilities as tools can still require too much code. My own album module didn't expose tools, and making its existing capabilities available to an AI assistant took about 1,000 additional lines of code.

But once those tools were available, the value became obvious. Adding MCP support has already changed how I manage the more than 10,000 photos on my site. Tasks that used to take a lot of time can now be done much faster and more accurately with an AI assistant, while Drupal still manages the content, permissions, and workflows underneath.

That experience reinforced something I wrote about in AI and the great CMS unbundling : AI can take on more of the execution work while Drupal remains the control layer. I expect more organizations will want to manage parts of their sites through AI assistants. AI can make complex tasks much faster and easier without giving up the structure, governance, and safeguards that Drupal provides.

I believe thousands of module developers will eventually want to expose their capabilities in the same way, so I've been working with Matt Glaman to make it much easier. Matt has been developing a change to the Tool API that lets developers expose existing PHP methods as tools using attributes.

The idea is simple: add PHP attributes to an existing method to describe its name, purpose, inputs and outputs. In my album module, roughly 1,000 lines of integration code became about 20 attributes. My site already uses the experimental branch, and we're working to get it merged into the Tool module proper.

And this isn't only about AI. The same tools can be called by AI assistants over MCP, by other applications over HTTP, or used to generate schemas for JavaScript components and connect Drupal modules to workflow systems like ECA , FlowDrop , and Maestro . The video below shows FlowDrop using capabilities exposed by my album module:

In the last part of my keynote, I came back to Drupal's reputation gap. We can make enormous progress with Drupal, but that doesn't automatically change what people or AI agents think of it. For example, an AI coding agent I tested in June didn't even mention Drupal CMS or Site Templates when it evaluated Drupal.

Over the past few years, much of my personal focus has been on accelerating innovation in Drupal. That work is paying off, and we have real product momentum. I'm now shifting more of my attention to the other side of the equation: making sure people see what we've built, understand what has changed, and know why it matters.

So I announced the Drupal Advocacy Program , led by the Drupal Association.

Drupal already has a contribution credit system. It recognizes the people who contribute to Drupal and the organizations that support their work. For businesses, those credits also help determine visibility in the Drupal marketplace. Until now, we've been much better at recognizing technical contributions and financial support than advocacy work.

The new Drupal Advocacy Program will change that. Advocacy work can now earn contribution credit, and work that reaches people outside the existing Drupal community can earn more weight.

If we want to close Drupal's reputation gap, we can't only talk to people who already know Drupal well. We need more talks at external events, articles in broader publications, customer stories, demos, tutorials, and other work that helps people see what Drupal can do today.

Blue Drop Labs is a good example of what I mean. The day after the DriesNote, they published a post on building a website with Drupal CMS and Canvas Headless . The project itself was already live, but they quickly turned that work into a story others could learn from, with demos showing how editors and developers work with Drupal today.

That is exactly what I mean by "talking louder". There is already a lot of impressive Drupal work happening. We need to do a better job of showing it to the world.

I was a little nervous about announcing the Advocacy Program. We've wrestled with Drupal's reputation gap for a long time, and I felt we needed to do more than acknowledge it. Using contribution credit to reward advocacy was a concrete way to change the incentives, but I wasn't sure how the community would react.

It turned out to be one of the best-received announcements of the keynote. That response gave me confidence that people were ready to act on the reputation gap, not just recognize it.

items.title: Clean up begins after French riots but police remain
items.summary: Outside of Paris, Marseille saw some of the worst damage, with shop owners reporting more than 600 premises having been looted.
items.content:
Following a weekend of intense rioting across France, a clean up operation has begun - but tensions remain, with police still in position and a curfew in place in some big cities.

Outside of Paris, Marseille saw some of the worst damage, with shop owners reporting more than 600 premises having been looted.

From the port city in southern France, the BBC's Nick Beake explains some of the factors behind the protests.

items.title: Curfew imposed in parts of central Paris and other cities after rioting across France
items.summary: It comes after the country's interior minister admits that police "lost control" in some cities.
items.content:
French authorities have imposed overnight curfews in parts of central Paris and other cities after a weekend of riots and looting across the country.

Police in Paris said a curfew would be in force between 23:00 local time (21:00 GMT) and 06:00 in Place de la République, where protesters had gathered over the weekend, and the Les Halles shopping area.

A ban on unauthorised gatherings has also been imposed in several other parts of the city centre.

Partial curfews variously restricting the movement of young people and gatherings were announced for cities including Marseille, Bordeaux, Nice and Lyon in the south as well as Lille and other towns in the north.

Earlier Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez, who has been strongly criticised by opposition politicians over the preparedness for the disorder but whose resignation was rejected by President Emmanuel Macron, admitted police had "lost control" in some cities.

The protests began last month with students demanding better school conditions, but they have since escalated to take in a broader range of concerns, with numbers at demonstrations this weekend bolstered by trade unions and various protest groups.

More than 2,500 people have been arrested, officials said. One demonstrator's hand was blown off by a police crowd-control grenade, according to the AFP news agency. About 1,000 police officers were injured.

Following a crisis meeting on Monday, the prime minister said local mayors were being given the power to implement curfews "where they need", without specifying which cities where they would be enforced.

Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu, who did not rule out imposing a state of emergency in the country, said the government would also set aside money to help affected areas recover from the damage, and the funding would be recovered from those behind the violence.

"There will be a law that will be put in place to find ways of making sure that those who have damaged properties will have to pay," Lecornu said.

He also announced a partial unemployment fund for those who could not work as a result of the riots and looting.

Meanwhile, Nuñez said 200 investigators were analysing CCTV footage to try to identify possible ringleaders.

He attempted to resign on Sunday, but Macron refused "given the need for continued command of law enforcement", the Élysée Palace said.

The statement said Nuñez should be transparent over what Macron called "intelligence and foresight failings".

More than 2,000 shops and other businesses have been directly impacted by the weekend's violence, the head of France's Chambers of Commerce and Industry (CCI) says.

Its head Alain Di Crescenzo told France's broadcaster RTL that damage from the riots was estimated at "hundreds of millions of euros".

Jean-Luc Chauvin, the president of the CCI's Marseille branch, told the BBC that many of the city's shop owners were in "deep distress" and fear for their survival.

Looted goods have been listed on certain selling platforms, two French government ministers said. A Vinted spokesperson said the sale or solicitation of stolen goods was "strictly prohibited".

"Since this weekend, our teams have taken immediate action to identify and remove listings linked to the looting, and we have stepped up monitoring of suspicious listings," it said.

Some 550,000 demonstrators took to the streets over the weekend for protests against rising fuel prices, the cost of living and deteriorating public services, including schools.

Groups of rioters, some dressed in black and wearing masks and balaclavas, were seen setting fire to cars and buildings and looting businesses in Paris, Marseille and other cities and smaller towns.

In the central city of Limoges, the ornate 19th Century city hall was gutted by a fire started by rioters on Saturday, its clock tower and roof collapsing as the flames took hold.

The US Embassy in France has issued an alert advising its citizens to avoid areas affected by the recent demonstrations.

The warning says to "exercise caution" if they find themselves close to large gatherings. China and Germany have issued similar warnings.

Some politicians have accused the left-wing La France Insoumise party of playing a role in the violence, with Lecornu alleging in an earlier news conference that some groups "want to create chaos in our country up until the presidential elections".

The party's leader Jean-Luc Mélenchon, who will stand in next year's presidential election, responded by calling for the French PM to "prove his accusation" or "apologise, shut up, and stop stoking disorder".

Katya Adler: France's government under pressure after weekend of widespread violence

Are student protests being manipulated ahead of France's presidential election?

Burnt out cars and shattered glass on Paris streets after protests turn to riots and looting

items.title: Ex-OpenAI worker accused of planting device had Saudi support, says court filing
items.summary: The Saudi government did not immediately respond to BBC requests for comment.
items.content:
A Saudi national charged with secretly planting a recording device in one of OpenAI's meeting rooms has been accused of having "considerable support" from the Saudi government, according to a court filing , external in California.

US prosecutors claimed Abdulrahman Alfozan, who worked for the AI firm, was in "frequent communication... with a member of the Saudi royal family", and say a member of the country's military paid for a one-way flight to Saudi Arabia for his wife and son after his arrest.

The 35-year-old engineer was on Monday deemed a flight risk and denied bail, pending trial.

The Saudi government did not immediately respond to BBC requests for comment.

Alfozan had worked at OpenAI for around a year before he allegedly made his attempt to plant an audio recorder.

The AI company discovered the device, which was plugged into the back of a TV in a conference meeting room and covered up with toilet paper, on 30 September.

A camera was placed in the room and on 5 October, Alfozan was filmed entering and appearing to look behind the television where the audio recorder had been inserted.

He was arrested by the FBI on 9 October and his contract with OpenAI was terminated.

The court filing claimed the suspect's alleged conduct could pose "a danger to the national security of the United States", because executives from the tech firm met with government officials in the room during the days the device was believed to have been installed.

It said Alfozan's arrest came three days before he was scheduled to fly from San Francisco to Riyadh on a one-way itinerary with his wife and son.

Following the arrest, the document claims the defendant's wife told FBI agents who interviewed her that "her US visa was expiring" and so she and her son were "permanently moving back to Saudi Arabia", and her husband intended to do the same.

On 10 October, the day after Alfozan was arrested, his wife and son flew from San Francisco to Doha, Qatar. They travelled on a one-way business class ticket booked and paid for by a Saudi military official.

"Ultimately, the defendant has little incentive to remain in the United States to see this case through," the prosecutors argued.

US district judge Alex Tse on Monday denied Alfozan's attorneys request for his release on bail, saying "there is a risk of non-appearance that is significant".

Alfozan was scheduled to ‌appear ⁠in federal court in San Francisco later on Monday. If convicted, he faces a maximum penalty of five years in prison and a $250,000 (£188,000) fine.

items.title: OpenBSD 8.0 release will have inteldrm/radeondrm/amdgpu drivers from Linux 6.18
items.summary: Article URL: https://bsd.network/@brynet/117407035545900963 Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50158138 Points: 79 # Comments: 10
items.content:
Clang/LLVM 22 is now OpenBSD's base compiler on clang architectures, including updated libc++{,abi}, compiler-rt & libunwind support libraries.

OpenBSD/sparc64 switches to Clang by default! This was the last significant architecture to switch. This makes OpenBSD the only operating system to support sparc64 with a modern toolchain.

Since 7.9, Jonathan Gray (jsg@) has continued to update the drm graphics stack (inteldrm/radeondrm/amdgpu) bringing OpenBSD 8.0 to Linux 6.18.y/6.18.53, adding driver support for Intel Arc A-Series (DG2/Alchemist) cards.

Increased KVA (kernel virtual addresses) on amd64 (to 512G) now allows mapping more than 4G of VRAM (for example, GPU compute w/ Vulkan)

After a ton of work in Edmonton by Mike Larkin (mlarkin@) and Dave Voutila (dv@), OpenBSD vmm/vmd(8) now supports SMP guests up to 64 VCPUs per VM! ​ 🎉​

OpenBSD 8.0 adds qwz(4), new WiFi driver for Qualcomm WCN7850 "ath12k" devices.

A new driver, sambat(4), for monitoring battery status, cycle count/charge info on Samsung Galaxy Book4 Edge (Snapdragon arm64) machines.

Accelerated swap encryption on amd64 and arm64 by using AES CPU instructions.

OpenBSD/arm64 and OpenBSD/riscv64 boards can now heartbeat blinking LEDs to show system load averages.

See also rsadowski@'s report: https:// rsadowski.de/posts/2026/w2k26- edmonton-openbsd-hackathon/

If you found my post at all engaging/useful, please consider supporting me. I post about OpenBSD often. ​

@ brynet that is so cool #BSD is full of so much great stuff, wish I could switch my hubby easily to it for gaming

@ brynet OpenBSD is the only OS I would contemplate running on an internet-facing host. So easy to keep it patched and updated!

@ brynet I wish I still had my UltraSPARC box. With BlueSCSI, I could have kept it running.

items.title: Serie A: doppietta di Simeone, il Torino passa a Parma con un tris
items.summary: Si è giocata la settima giornata di campionato. Monza show al Brianteo, poker al Cagliari
items.content:
Con una partenza a razzo il Torino espugna il Tardini e festeggia la seconda vittoria consecutiva: doppio Simeone più Adams, per il Parma è notte fonda. Gilardino, al debutto casalingo sulla panchina crociata, propone un 5-3-2 con Bernabè in regia e la coppia Tourè-Romero davanti. Abate si schiera a specchio con il 3-5-2 e rilancia Vlasic dal primo minuto. Dopo un minuto i granata guadagnano il primo corner, non è soltanto un'impressione, sono partiti forte e infatti al 4' passano. Azione in uscita dalla difesa, sponda di Simeone a centrocampo, Belghali sfreccia sulla destra e mette in mezzo: il Cholito segna di piatto al volo sul secondo palo. L'argentino si sblocca dopo sei giornate a secco, il Parma resta a guardare. I crociati soffrono la velocità delle fasce granata, a sinistra Cacciamani scappa e Britschgi non lo tiene. Il raddoppio è nell'aria: arriva al 24' quando Adams è tutto solo sotto porta e corregge in rete un tiro di Vlasic deviato da un difensore.

Check var, rete valida: esultano i pochi presenti nel settore ospiti, la curva nord del Tardini grida ai crociati di tirare fuori gli attributi. La reazione tarda, la prima occasione dei padroni di casa è un regalo e arriva al 34' da un errato disimpegno di Perri che rinvia corto sui piedi di Delprato: il pallone giunge a Fabbian che serve Romero in area, la girata rasoterra non è abbastanza angolata e il portiere si riscatta deviando in tuffo. Sugli sviluppi dell'azione altra uscita maldestra dei granata, Tourè vede Perri fuori dai pali ma il suo pallonetto finisce nelle mani del portiere. Troppo poco, il Parma esce tra i fischi all'intervallo. Gilardino cambia: fuori Diego Carlos e Fabbian, dentro Drobnic e Lontani, i crociati passano al 3-4-2-1. Cambio modulo, cambia l'approccio, sembra iniziare un'altra partita: al 3' cross di Bernabè ma Tourè non inquadra la porta di testa. Due minuti dopo Lontani sfiora la traversa col destro dopo aver vinto un rimpallo all'ingresso in area. Altra chance per Romero, l'argentino anticipa tutti ma calcia alto da buona posizione, Il Toro regge, il Parma rifiata e Simeone cala il tris granata: botta da 25 metri, Corvi non impeccabile è battuto. Dalla curva gialloblù inizia la contestazione alla società. Nel finale resta solo un gol annullato al subentrato Frigan, non è serata per gli emiliani. Un'ottima mezzora, un secondo tempo di lotta: il Toro ha qualità e carattere, tre punti meritati. Il Parma del dopo Cuesta è un enigma: due sconfitte, sei reti subite e zero fatte nelle ultime due partite, la classifica da zona retrocessione non mente.

items.title: Putting Linux on my RTX Spark laptop because I don't have a Microsoft account
items.summary: Article URL: https://josie.lol/blog/linux-rtx-spark Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50158100 Points: 173 # Comments: 75
items.content:
tl;dr - boo hoo microsoft bad. Arch Linux works, keeps up with Windows in 7-Zip, and reports the same 116.0 GiB memory pool to the OS and CUDA. My initial bootable setup and patches are here . This is for the ASUS ProArt P16 H7607BA-SE033W: the 128 GB RAM configuration with 6,144 CUDA cores and a 2 TB SSD.

When rumours started circulating about a laptop with over 100 GiB of RAM the GPU could access, I started thinking about all the things I could build on it and all the optimisations I could spend far too long playing with. I'm very pro open-weight models. Being able to run things locally and mess around with RL, quantisation and fine-tuning on a laptop would be sick. I already publish my own GGUF quants on Hugging Face , with over 160,000 downloads in the past month.

So I was less pleased to find out about the Windows-only official support . There are plenty of reasons to hate Windows. Mine include the privacy concessions during setup , the years spent waiting for Microsoft to let people put the taskbar on the side of the screen again , and the advertising . That last link is a collage of real Windows promotions, courtesy of Pureinfotech . You get it. I can go on forever, so let me stay on topic.

Arch is my preferred distribution, and I'm on the Arch staff as a package maintainer . I already put it on IBM mainframes ( my FOSDEM slides ), so it was always going to be my starting point here. This build uses Arch Linux ARM , the separate project that ports Arch packages to ARM, with the hardware support added on top.

NVIDIA has been doing kernel work for Ubuntu, which gave me a starting point. I incorporated that, fixed the ACPI override allocation and framebuffer mapping needed to get a console, and worked out the ACPI overrides from the laptop's own tables (thanks astra official places on the internet (pls don't sue me computer companies). Keyboard support needed a patched hid-asus , and audio needed its own machine driver.

I put this together into a bootable USB and extended upstream Archinstall 4.5 to install the hardware support. The repo has the build scripts and patches , including the steps to dump your own ACPI tables and extract the speaker firmware from ASUS's driver package locally. Mine runs firmware H7607BA.300.

The build inputs are hash pinned. The hardware packages I put together over the weekend are signed with my Arch Linux Package Maintainer key, and the ACPI overrides come from the laptop itself.

The display runs at 3840 × 2400 and 120 Hz, and I use NetworkManager, PipeWire, and rootless Podman with NVIDIA CDI. The installer holds the kernel, NVIDIA, power-management and firmware packages with IgnorePkg , while ordinary packages keep updating from Arch Linux ARM.

I ran the suite on October 19 on native Arch Linux ARM, with kernel 7.0.0-1022-nvidia and NVIDIA driver 615.78.08 . The laptop was plugged in with the performance profile selected. For the CPU comparison, I used published Windows results.

The CPU test is native ARM64 7-Zip 26.04 with a fixed 32 MiB dictionary. I ran one warmup and three measured passes at each thread count, then took the medians:

StorageReview tested a 128 GB HP OmniBook Ultra 16 with the same 20-core N1X, running native Windows ARM64 binaries. They report 7-Zip ratings in GIPS, so I divided the MIPS ratings in my raw logs by 1,000 to match. Higher is better.

Single-thread is basically a tie. With all 20 threads, my Linux setup is about 5% ahead on compression and 3% ahead on decompression. The HP review doesn't specify its 7-Zip version or dictionary size, so these percentages compare the two laptop setups.

ComputerBase also tested a ProArt P16 with the 20-core N1X . Converted to GIPS, its Windows 7-Zip score was 155.774; the median total from my three runs was 157.084. Their result sits inside my three-run range of 155.759 to 157.193 GIPS. Their machine was the 64 GB configuration and ran 7-Zip 26.00, and the chart doesn't give the dictionary size.

The memory is a bigger flex. My Linux run reports 116.0 GiB as both system RAM and CUDA's total, from the same physical pool. Windows divides the RAM into dedicated GPU, shared, and CPU-only regions . CPU workloads can't use the dedicated GPU region, and GPU allocations can't use the CPU-only region.

The Windows NVIDIA app lets you change the dedicated reservation and reboot; Frandroid's 128 GB ProArt P16 reached 96 GiB . CUDA can go beyond that by allocating from shared RAM , subject to Windows' memory budget.

With a 91 GiB dedicated reservation, Frandroid's Windows setup reported a CUDA total of 109.7 GiB, including shared memory. My Linux setup reported 116.0 GiB, about 6.3 GiB more. What I care about is having the large pool available for CPU work too, without moving the reservation slider and rebooting between workloads.

I ran NVIDIA's Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP4-Local checkpoint through vLLM with B12X CUDA kernels in a native ARM64 container, using mixed quantization and FP8 KV cache. I turned off thinking for this run.

Before loading the model, Linux reported 110.9 GiB of available RAM. vLLM logged 68.2 GiB for model loading and allocated another 21.1 GiB to the KV cache. That's nearly 90 GiB allocated to the model and KV cache on a laptop.

Model loading and compilation took about 16 minutes before the first request. The timings below start after warmup. PLE embedding tables are backed by disk and benefit from a warm page cache; other components use CPU offload. CUDA handles inference, with some of the model outside GPU memory.

I gave Qwen two buggy Python helpers to review, a long incident log with one failed operation to find, and a payment note to turn into JSON. Each task ran three times after warmup, with known answers to check against. I wanted to know how long I'd wait and whether it returned the right fields.

The incident task read nearly 10,000 tokens and returned the correct request, cause, and next action in under 6 s. Its answer was only 39 tokens long, which comes to 6.8 tokens/s over the whole request. Most of the wait went into processing the prompt, so for this task the response time tells me more than the tokens/s figure.

For code review, I estimated generation speed as (output tokens − 1) / (response time − time to first token) , with both times in seconds. This includes stream overhead. Frandroid ran Qwen3.8-Flash-Next coding tasks on its Windows ProArt :

Both ProArt setups are around 30 tokens/s. For inference, Frandroid used an 85 GiB dedicated reservation and a context limit of 262,144 tokens; my context limit was 32,768 tokens. The prompts, quants, runtimes, and timing methods differ. This compares two working configurations; it doesn't isolate the effect of the OS.

I also sent four code reviews at once. The median batch finished in 5.314 s, producing 86.6 output tokens/s across all four requests combined. That rate includes prompt processing and response overhead. All 12 answers passed over three batches.

Then I left it cycling through the three tasks, one request at a time, for ten minutes. It finished 150 requests, 50 of each, and every answer passed the checks. Median response times were 4.036 s for code review, 5.921 s for the log, and 2.046 s for extraction. Comparing the first ten and last ten repetitions of each task, median response times grew by less than 1.6%.

All 171 measured responses passed the checks. That's three prompts repeated with deterministic decoding; the code-review check verifies the regression outputs. I kept every answer and raw event stream and checked them against the summaries.
